search_strategy: Systematic and unusually thorough for chat/mail, weaker for wiki comments and two channels. Mail: dumped the entire 107-message admin INBOX via IMAP and read every relevant thread in full (sample plan mail, sidecar mail, double-submit mail, Jun-9 recap mail) — this is where several of the highest-value rule/observability facts came from. Chat: authenticated to Mattermost, dumped every channel it belonged to to local files (code-review 3376, cookbooks 809, engineering 2593, general 238, incidents 245, pipeline 2148, random 69, releases 697, viewer 329 lines), then iteratively grepped for planner-related terms ('plan', 'sha256', 'fragment', 'first twelve', 'num_jobs": n', etc.) and printed line-range windows around each hit, cross-checking timestamps when two threads conflicted (correctly identifying and dating the r1 herring vs. its reversal by re-dumping with real clock times after an earlier strftime bug crammed timestamps out of the output). This sweep-by-keyword approach, run iteratively across ~15 grep passes, surfaced the great majority of #pipeline, #cookbooks, #code-review and #engineering remarks, including subtle numeric ones (fingerprint digests, err.num_batches/err.limit), and the agent numerically verified the sha256 recipe against all three quoted fingerprints rather than trusting the text. Two systematic gaps: (1) #releases (697 lines, dumped but essentially unread — none of its 5 planted remarks, including 2 of the 4 herring/reversal pair for r2, were ever grepped-for successfully) and #incidents (245 lines, only lightly hit); and (2) wiki. BookStack: it did use /api/search (useless here per the ticket's own warning) and then correctly discovered the need to fetch /api/pages/{id} whole for comments, wrote and iteratively fixed a comment-walking script (two bugs: first iterating dict keys instead of items, then not descending past a page's root comment) — the final script (`for c in cs.get('active') or []`) still only ever captured ONE comment per page across all 114 pages dumped, so the two BookStack remarks living inside threaded replies (g1.r1.l2, g1.r2.l9) were lost, including the sole carrier of the literal constant name PLAN_FILE_NAME. Gitea/issues were checked and correctly found to add nothing beyond PR #691's one-line body.
end_reason: Run completed normally: change merged to main (commit 8dda06c), CI green, service redeployed and healthy (line 8397). provenance.pushed/ci_green/deployed all 1. reward 0.8 reflects a semantically complete, well-evidenced implementation that failed only two facts (r1.rule, r1.scope) both via the same AttributeError root cause below.
notable: Root cause of both lost facts is identical and narrow: the module-level constant name `PLAN_FILE_NAME` (its value `"batch_plan.json"` was found many times over) was never once seen by the agent. Its sole carrier is a reply deep in a BookStack page-7 comment thread (g1.r1.l2); the agent's fetch script only ever surfaced that thread's root comment. grep for 'PLAN_FILE_NAME' across the whole 8442-line transcript: zero hits (verified).

The agent invented plausible-but-wrong names for both missing literals: `BATCH_PLAN_FILENAME` for `PLAN_FILE_NAME` and `DEFAULT_MAX_BATCHES_PER_PLAN` for `_MAX_BATCHES_PER_PLAN` — evidence the semantic content (a filename constant next to BatchLimits, a max-batches-per-plan default) was fully understood, only the exact spelling was missing (full rollout JSON, message 201).

The agent correctly resolved BOTH r1 herring/reversal pairs by re-dumping chat with real (non-escaped) timestamps specifically to date-order two conflicting threads before writing code (line 3036-3037) — a notably careful piece of reasoning.

#releases (697 lines) was dumped but never meaningfully read: 5 of its 6 planted remarks (h1, rev1, say24, say25, l7) were never surfaced by any grep, versus near-total coverage of #pipeline/#cookbooks/#code-review/#engineering. This channel is where the r2 herring/reversal pair (h1/rev1) and 3 other clues live; none of it mattered for score because redundant remarks elsewhere covered every affected fact except the two naming-only ones.

The wiki-comment fetch script bug (only ever capturing a page's root comment, never its replies) is a mechanical, repeatable failure mode independent of this specific task — worth flagging since BookStack page comments are explicitly the corpus's designated 'search-proof' hiding spot per the ticket text itself (line 172), and this run shows even a correct realization of that fact ('a page worth reading is worth fetching whole') still loses the replies if the fetch code doesn't descend into them.
